== 1
# CLI commands
== 3
**Source:** `crates/cli/src/main.rs`, `crates/cli/src/config.rs`, `crates/cli/src/output.rs`, `crates/cli/src/commands/mod.rs`, `crates/cli/src/commands/extract.rs`, `crates/cli/src/commands/check.rs`, `crates/cli/src/commands/watch.rs`, `crates/cli/src/commands/inspect.rs`, `crates/cli/src/commands/schema.rs`, `crates/cli/src/commands/completions.rs`, `crates/cli/AGENTS.md`
== 5
This is the thin command layer sitting on top of `caliper-docgen-core::pipeline`. It owns nothing about extraction — only argument parsing, calling into the pipeline, formatting output, and deciding the process exit code. Per `crates/cli/AGENTS.md`: "no extraction logic," "no `println!` in command handlers" outside `output.rs`/tracing, and config loading must avoid command injection.
== 20
`main()` (`main.rs:175-203`) is the **sole `std::process::exit` call site** in the crate. Every command handler returns a `Result<i32>` (or hardcodes `0` inline for the three that don't call the pipeline), and `main()` maps a non-zero return to `process::exit(exit_code)` after the match. This is stated explicitly in `cmd_extract`'s doc comment (`extract.rs:6-9`) and repeated in `cmd_check`'s (`check.rs:6-8`): keeping the exit decision out of command handlers is what makes it testable — `cmd_extract`/`cmd_check`/`cmd_inspect`/`cmd_watch` all have unit tests that call the handler directly and assert on the returned `i32`, without needing a subprocess harness or capturing a real process exit.
== 28
3. **`docgen.config.ts`'s path is passed to the `node` subprocess via the `__DOCGEN_CONFIG_PATH` environment variable, never interpolated into the script string.** `config.rs:117-126` builds a fixed script body (`"import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url'; const p = process.env.__DOCGEN_CONFIG_PATH; ..."`) and sets the actual path with `.env("__DOCGEN_CONFIG_PATH", path)`. This is a security-critical invariant, not a style preference: `crates/cli/AGENTS.md` calls it out by name — "The config file path is passed via env var, not embedded in a shell string — command injection risk otherwise." A user-controlled or attacker-controlled path (e.g. a filename containing `` ` `` or `${...}` sequences, or `--config` pointed at a crafted location) must never be able to inject JavaScript into the script `node` evaluates. If a future change reformats this script with `format!("...{path}...")` instead of the env var, that reintroduces the injection.
== 30
4. **A `docgen.config.ts` that exists but fails to load is a hard error, not a silent fallback to defaults.** `try_load_config` (`config.rs:112-177`) surfaces node/tsx's real stderr on evaluation failure, and `into_pipeline_options` (`config.rs:33`) rejects unknown fields (`deny_unknown_fields`, which includes options that were removed for doing nothing) and unrecognized `htmlAttributes` strings by name rather than defaulting. This is AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6 ("never fail silently") applied at the config layer: a config the user explicitly wrote getting quietly ignored due to a typo would be a plausible-looking but wrong result forever, and the regression tests for this (`config_schema_rejects_options_that_were_removed_for_doing_nothing`, `config_schema_rejects_a_typo_d_html_attributes_instead_of_defaulting`, `try_load_config_surfaces_the_real_syntax_error_not_just_an_exit_status`) pin it.
== 32
5. **`ExtractionOutput::exit_code(strict: bool) -> i32` is the single source of truth for the 0/1/2 exit-code mapping, and every command that reports it must call this method rather than re-deriving the check.** The mapping (`core/types/output.rs:42-55`): `Error` present → `2`; `Warning` present and `strict` → `1`; `Warning` present and not `strict` → `0`; `Info`-only or clean → `0`. `extract`, `check`, `watch`, and `inspect` all now call this one method (see Locked Design Decisions — this was a real duplication bug, fixed).
== 34
6. **`--json` on `extract` must still run the same `exit_code(false)` check as the human-readable path — it must not return early.** `extract.rs:44-68`: the `if args.json { ... }` branch prints and falls through to the same `Ok(output.exit_code(false))` at the bottom of the function rather than having its own early `return Ok(0)`. The regression test `json_mode_still_returns_the_error_exit_code` (`extract.rs:176-183`) is named directly after the adversarial-review finding this fixed: `--json` used to return before the exit-code check ran, so `extract --json` always exited `0` even on a hard error — "the one signal CI actually depends on," per the test's own comment.
== 36
7. **`watch`'s exit code must come from the session's cumulative snapshot, not the current file-change event's own diagnostics.** `watch.rs:142-143` explicitly sources `watch_exit_code` from `session_inner.snapshot()` — the whole tree's current diagnostic state — rather than from just the `update` returned by `update_file(&utf8)` for this one edit. The comment at that call site spells out why: sourcing from the per-event delta would let a clean edit to file A reset the tracked exit code to 0 even though file B, untouched in this event, still has an unresolved error.
== 38
8. **`watch`'s output-file writes are atomic (`write_atomic`, `watch.rs:17-39`): temp file in the same directory, then `rename`.** A mid-write failure (disk full, permission revoked) must never leave the `--out` path holding truncated JSON, since some other process (a bundler, a dev-server file watcher) may be reading that path concurrently and can't tell a half-written file from a valid empty one.
== 44
11. **`inspect` must still surface Error-severity diagnostics found elsewhere in the source tree, even when the specifically-inspected component is clean.** `inspect.rs:82` calls `output.exit_code(false)` unconditionally after a successful component lookup, using the full `output` from `pipeline::extract`, not a filtered view scoped to just `args.component`. The test `inspect_surfaces_error_exit_code_from_diagnostics_elsewhere_in_the_tree` pins this down with a fixture where the inspected component (`Comp.tsx`) is valid but a sibling file (`Bad.tsx`) has a parse error, asserting exit code `2`.
== 52
**`node`/`tsx` is spawned with `command.current_dir(dir)` set to the _config file's own directory_, not the CLI's invocation `cwd`.** (`config.rs:130-137`.) This matters for two real scenarios the comment names directly: `--config ../other-project/docgen.config.ts` pointing outside the current project, and a project whose `tsx` devDependency isn't hoisted to wherever the caller happened to invoke the CLI from. Resolving `tsx` (and anything the config file itself imports) relative to the config file's directory, via Node's own ancestor-walking package resolution, is what makes both cases work. Don't "simplify" this to always use the CLI's own `cwd`.
== 56
**`watch`'s keyboard-input thread calls `std::process::exit(0)` directly on `q`/ctrl-c** (`watch.rs:101-104`), which is the one deliberate exception to Invariant 1. It's spawned as a detached `std::thread::spawn` reading raw terminal events in a loop with no owned `JoinHandle` the main thread waits on — there's no `Result<i32>` return path back to `main()` from inside that thread, and disabling raw mode (`crossterm::terminal::disable_raw_mode()`) before exiting is itself part of why the exit happens inline rather than via a channel-and-return.
== 58
**`extract --json` intentionally ignores `--out`/`--format`.** `ExtractArgs::json`'s doc comment (`main.rs:103-107`) states this precisely: `--json` is "the canonical schema, compact, always to stdout, ignoring --out/--format (which govern the human/RDT paths below), and suppresses the human-readable summary/diagnostics." This is a deliberate two-mode split (machine-readable canonical vs. human/RDT-formatted), not an oversight where `--json --out foo.json` should have written to the file — it never will, by design.
== 64
The `composes` field (react-docgen's own "props come from this type, listed by name instead of flattened" fallback for unresolvable types) was populated by the resolver but **used to be silently dropped by `serialize_rdt`** — the `rdt_output_includes_composes` test (`extract.rs:202-227`) and its comment block point at the resolver-side fix in `pipeline::tests::test_unresolvable_intersection_member_records_raw_type_in_composes` as the other half of that bug. If a new `ComponentEntry` field is ever added on the core side, check `pipeline::rdt` by hand — nothing enforces that every core field round-trips into this hand-written serializer, which is exactly the class of bug `composes` fell into.
== 68
`schema_value()` (`schema.rs:7-99`) is a **hand-maintained** JSON Schema for `ExtractionOutput` — there's no `#[derive(JsonSchema)]` generating it from the real struct. The module doc comment names this precedent ("Hand-maintained per ADR-0002-style precedent") and pairs it with `schema_covers_every_field_name_the_real_output_serializes` (`schema.rs:117-211`), which builds a fully-populated real `ExtractionOutput`, serializes it, walks every key name that appears in the real JSON, and asserts each one appears somewhere in the hand-written schema string. This is a **name-presence check, not a shape/type check** — it would catch a field being added to `ComponentEntry` and forgotten in `schema_value()`, but it would not catch the schema describing the wrong _type_ for a field that already has the right _name_. Extending a field's type without touching its name passes this test silently.
== 70
## No language server
== 72
A `lsp` subcommand existed as a scaffold (framing and the initialize/shutdown/exit lifecycle, `hoverProvider: false`) and was removed: editors already get hover and completion from the TypeScript language server, and the value caliper adds, the documentation view of a component, is served to tools through the lazy session API instead. The bounded-framing code that `crates/tsc-client` ported from it lives on there.
== 78
- **`--json` on `extract` has no equivalent on `check`'s already-JSON-capable path worth double-checking for consistency** — `check --json` (`check.rs:21-22`) emits `output.diagnostics` directly (an array), while `extract --json` (`extract.rs:45-46`) emits the full `ExtractionOutput` (an object). These are two different JSON shapes under the same flag name across two commands; not a bug (each is documented for its own command), but worth knowing before assuming `--json` means the same payload shape everywhere in this CLI.

This is AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6 ("never fail silently") applied at the config layer: a config the user explicitly wrote getting quietly ignored due to a typo would be a plausible-looking but wrong result forever, and the regression tests for this (`config_schema_rejects_options_that_were_removed_for_doing_nothing`, `config_schema_rejects_a_typo_d_html_attributes_instead_of_defaulting`, `try_load_config_surfaces_the_real_syntax_error_not_just_an_exit_status`) pin it.
== 32
5. **`ExtractionOutput::exit_code(strict: bool) -> i32` is the single source of truth for the 0/1/2 exit-code mapping, and every command that reports it must call this method rather than re-deriving the check.** The mapping (`core/types/output.rs:42-55`): `Error` present → `2`; `Warning` present and `strict` → `1`; `Warning` present and not `strict` → `0`; `Info`-only or clean → `0`. `extract`, `check`, `watch`, and `inspect` all now call this one method (see Locked Design Decisions — this was a real duplication bug, fixed).
== 34
6. **`--json` on `extract` must still run the same `exit_code(false)` check as the human-readable path — it must not return early.** `extract.rs:44-68`: the `if args.json { ... }` branch prints and falls through to the same `Ok(output.exit_code(false))` at the bottom of the function rather than having its own early `return Ok(0)`. The regression test `json_mode_still_returns_the_error_exit_code` (`extract.rs:176-183`) is named directly after the adversarial-review finding this fixed: `--json` used to return before the exit-code check ran, so `extract --json` always exited `0` even on a hard error — "the one signal CI actually depends on," per the test's own comment.
== 36
7. **`watch`'s exit code must come from the session's cumulative snapshot, not the current file-change event's own diagnostics.** `watch.rs:142-143` explicitly sources `watch_exit_code` from `session_inner.snapshot()` — the whole tree's current diagnostic state — rather than from just the `update` returned by `update_file(&utf8)` for this one edit. The comment at that call site spells out why: sourcing from the per-event delta would let a clean edit to file A reset the tracked exit code to 0 even though file B, untouched in this event, still has an unresolved error.
== 38
8. **`watch`'s output-file writes are atomic (`write_atomic`, `watch.rs:17-39`): temp file in the same directory, then `rename`.** A mid-write failure (disk full, permission revoked) must never leave the `--out` path holding truncated JSON, since some other process (a bundler, a dev-server file watcher) may be reading that path concurrently and can't tell a half-written file from a valid empty one.
== 44
11. **`inspect` must still surface Error-severity diagnostics found elsewhere in the source tree, even when the specifically-inspected component is clean.** `inspect.rs:82` calls `output.exit_code(false)` unconditionally after a successful component lookup, using the full `output` from `pipeline::extract`, not a filtered view scoped to just `args.component`. The test `inspect_surfaces_error_exit_code_from_diagnostics_elsewhere_in_the_tree` pins this down with a fixture where the inspected component (`Comp.tsx`) is valid but a sibling file (`Bad.tsx`) has a parse error, asserting exit code `2`.
== 52
**`node`/`tsx` is spawned with `command.current_dir(dir)` set to the _config file's own directory_, not the CLI's invocation `cwd`.** (`config.rs:130-137`.) This matters for two real scenarios the comment names directly: `--config ../other-project/docgen.config.ts` pointing outside the current project, and a project whose `tsx` devDependency isn't hoisted to wherever the caller happened to invoke the CLI from. Resolving `tsx` (and anything the config file itself imports) relative to the config file's directory, via Node's own ancestor-walking package resolution, is what makes both cases work. Don't "simplify" this to always use the CLI's own `cwd`.
== 56
**`watch`'s keyboard-input thread calls `std::process::exit(0)` directly on `q`/ctrl-c** (`watch.rs:101-104`), which is the one deliberate exception to Invariant 1. It's spawned as a detached `std::thread::spawn` reading raw terminal events in a loop with no owned `JoinHandle` the main thread waits on — there's no `Result<i32>` return path back to `main()` from inside that thread, and disabling raw mode (`crossterm::terminal::disable_raw_mode()`) before exiting is itself part of why the exit happens inline rather than via a channel-and-return.
== 58
**`extract --json` intentionally ignores `--out`/`--format`.** `ExtractArgs::json`'s doc comment (`main.rs:103-107`) states this precisely: `--json` is "the canonical schema, compact, always to stdout, ignoring --out/--format (which govern the human/RDT paths below), and suppresses the human-readable summary/diagnostics." This is a deliberate two-mode split (machine-readable canonical vs. human/RDT-formatted), not an oversight where `--json --out foo.json` should have written to the file — it never will, by design.
== 64
The `composes` field (react-docgen's own "props come from this type, listed by name instead of flattened" fallback for unresolvable types) was populated by the resolver but **used to be silently dropped by `serialize_rdt`** — the `rdt_output_includes_composes` test (`extract.rs:202-227`) and its comment block point at the resolver-side fix in `pipeline::tests::test_unresolvable_intersection_member_records_raw_type_in_composes` as the other half of that bug. If a new `ComponentEntry` field is ever added on the core side, check `pipeline::rdt` by hand — nothing enforces that every core field round-trips into this hand-written serializer, which is exactly the class of bug `composes` fell into.
== 68
`schema_value()` (`schema.rs:7-99`) is a **hand-maintained** JSON Schema for `ExtractionOutput` — there's no `#[derive(JsonSchema)]` generating it from the real struct. The module doc comment names this precedent ("Hand-maintained per ADR-0002-style precedent") and pairs it with `schema_covers_every_field_name_the_real_output_serializes` (`schema.rs:117-211`), which builds a fully-populated real `ExtractionOutput`, serializes it, walks every key name that appears in the real JSON, and asserts each one appears somewhere in the hand-written schema string. This is a **name-presence check, not a shape/type check** — it would catch a field being added to `ComponentEntry` and forgotten in `schema_value()`, but it would not catch the schema describing the wrong _type_ for a field that already has the right _name_. Extending a field's type without touching its name passes this test silently.
== 70
## No language server
== 72
A `lsp` subcommand existed as a scaffold (framing and the initialize/shutdown/exit lifecycle, `hoverProvider: false`) and was removed: editors already get hover and completion from the TypeScript language server, and the value caliper adds, the documentation view of a component, is served to tools through the lazy session API instead. The bounded-framing code that `crates/tsc-client` ported from it lives on there.
== 78
- **`--json` on `extract` has no equivalent on `check`'s already-JSON-capable path worth double-checking for consistency** — `check --json` (`check.rs:21-22`) emits `output.diagnostics` directly (an array), while `extract --json` (`extract.rs:45-46`) emits the full `ExtractionOutput` (an object). These are two different JSON shapes under the same flag name across two commands; not a bug (each is documented for its own command), but worth knowing before assuming `--json` means the same payload shape everywhere in this CLI.

95 1. **Component output keys are `display_name`, disambiguated to `"{name} ({file_path})"` on the 2nd+ occurrence of that name — this still collides for a genuine 3-way-or-more same-name-same-file duplicate.** Phase 5 tracks a `seen_names: HashMap<String, u32>` counter per base name; the _first_ occurrence gets the bare name, every later occurrence gets the disambiguated key. Since `file_path` is unique per file, two different libraries shipping a same-named `Button.tsx` never collide (each gets a distinct disambiguated key) — but three or more literal duplicate declarations of the same component in the _same file_ (`function Button() {}` repeated) all key identically after the first, and `components.insert` silently overwrites unless its `Option<ComponentEntry>` return is checked. It is checked (see `pipeline/mod.rs:456`), which is what turns this residual case into a `ComponentKeyCollision` diagnostic rather than a silent drop — but the entry itself is still lost from the map, only the _fact_ of the loss is preserved. See `test_duplicate_component_declarations_in_one_file_emit_a_collision_diagnostic`.

97 2. **`discover_files` must dedup identical canonical paths _before_ they become separate `ComponentMapping`s — the Phase-5 collision check alone cannot catch a 2-directory overlap.** Two overlapping `src_dirs` (e.g. `["./src", "./src/components"]`) walk the same physical file twice. Because the two resulting mappings key _differently_ under Invariant 1's numbering scheme (first occurrence → bare name, second → disambiguated name), they never collide at `insert` and would both silently appear as separate output entries. The actual fix is the `files.sort(); files.dedup();` at the end of `discover_files` (`discover.rs:94-95`), which only works because every path was canonicalized first — an uncanonicalized relative/absolute duplicate pair would sort non-adjacently and evade `dedup()`. See `test_overlapping_src_dirs_two_directories_deduplicates_without_a_duplicate_listing`.

105 6. **A cache-persistence failure (`DtsCache::save_to_disk`) must degrade to `DiagnosticSeverity::Info`, never `Warning`.** `Warning` would flip `docgen check --strict`'s exit code to 1 purely because the _next_ run will have to re-parse `.d.ts` files — extraction output for _this_ run is completely correct either way. This is a deliberate severity choice, not an oversight; the comment at `cache.rs:143-148` explicitly calls out this is the same class of spurious exit-code flip already fixed once elsewhere in the resolver.

16 - `ResolveState` (`types/global.rs:19`) is constructed fresh per `resolve_component` call via `ResolveState::default()` and threaded through every recursive call by `&mut` reference. It is **never** shared across components and carries no `Arc` — it's pure per-call mutable scratch state (visited-set, diagnostics accumulator, in-scope type params). If a future change tried to hoist `ResolveState` up to be shared across the rayon `.map()` (e.g. to dedupe diagnostics), that would silently corrupt cycle detection across unrelated components — the visited-set has no per-component reset mechanism, and two components racing on the same shared set would each see the other's visited entries and wrongly short-circuit.

84 ## Locked design decision: source-before-known-pattern precedence (P0-1)

86 `resolver/precedence.rs`'s `resolve_source_defined_or_known` is the **only** place either `chain.rs` or `named.rs` may implement "how does a bare type name resolve." It checks, in this exact order:

88 1. `resolve_to_canonical` — follow imports/re-exports/barrel files to the real declaring `(file, name)`.

90 3. `lookup_interface` at that canonical location.

93 **Why this order, and why it's locked:** a project can legitimately declare its own `interface SxProps { customSx: string }` that has nothing to do with MUI. If `known.rs`'s hardcoded SxProps shortcut were checked before the project's own source, that project-defined interface would be silently replaced by the opaque MUI shortcut — the component's real, resolvable prop (`customSx`) would vanish with no trace. `named.rs` always had this order right and documented it as intentional. `chain.rs`'s `extends`-clause path (used when a project's `interface Foo extends SomeName`) independently re-implemented the same sequence and got it backwards — checking `resolve_known` _before_ the project's own interface/alias lookup. Nothing tied the two orderings together, so `chain.rs` was free to drift the moment it was written. This is the confirmed P0-1 bug; `precedence.rs` was extracted specifically to make that drift structurally impossible — both call sites now share one function, so reordering one without the other can't happen again.

95 A regression test locks this at both the shared-function level (`precedence.rs`'s `source_defined_interface_wins_over_a_known_pattern_shortcut`) and end-to-end through the extends path (`mod.rs`'s `test_extends_clause_prefers_project_defined_sx_props_over_known_shortcut`).

97 **Documented residual divergence (not a bug, but don't call the two functions "unified"):** `chain.rs` and `named.rs` still differ in two respects the P0-1 fix didn't touch — `named.rs` checks React-builtin status _before_ canonical resolution, `chain.rs` checks it _after_ the known-pattern block; and `chain.rs` checks `is_ts_utility_type` very early (step 1, before known-pattern), while `named.rs`'s analogous check runs last (step 6, after interface/alias/known-pattern). Neither divergence reproduces the P0-1 shape (a user-defined type being shadowed by a shortcut), so they were explicitly left out of scope. If a future change touches either ordering, re-verify this claim rather than assuming it's still accurate — nothing in code flags it.

101 `PropType::Opaque`'s payload (`OpaqueDetail`, `types/output.rs:324`) is private outside its own module and has exactly two constructors:

153 

154 - **Generic substitution through nested builtin chains** (Ariakit `Props<T, O>` and 5 siblings) — `docs/benchmarks.md`, "Corsa-deferred" generic-parameter-substitution item.

155 - **`composes` as a stop-gap, not a fix** — `docs/benchmarks.md` explains `composes` population closes the _symptom_ (silent zero-props output) for type-checker-boundary failures, not the underlying inability to expand conditional/mapped/indexed-access types without a real checker.

156 - **Resolver precedence's two residual (non-P0-1) divergences** between `chain.rs` and `named.rs` (React-builtin-check ordering, `is_ts_utility_type` check ordering) — left open by the precedence extraction above.

157 - **The type of a value built by a call** (`z.infer<typeof schema>` with `const schema = z.object({ ... })`; a store, a hook's result). `typeof X` is a type here only for components, cva variants and `as const` arrays (and now `declare const X: readonly [...]`). TypeScript infers the call's generic arguments from its argument expression and then evaluates the library's conditional and mapped types; that needs the checker (ADR 0006), so the prop stays a named reference (`Event["name"]`) with an Info `OPAQUE_TYPE` diagnostic whose help names the remedy: declare the type where it is used, or `--experimental-semantic-types`. shadcn's `CopyButton.event` is the example.

158 

163 - **A generic interface/alias's own declared type parameters must be registered before its body is resolved**, via `ctx.global.interface_type_params` / `type_alias_params` feeding `state.in_scope_type_params` — otherwise `TData`, `T`, `U`, etc. read as unresolvable named types with a spurious warning instead of being recognized as expected, unexpandable placeholders (`test_generic_interface_own_type_params_suppress_diagnostic`).

20 The line the project actually draws, reverse-engineered from where each format lives: "terminal/display code" means code whose job is to _render for a human looking at a terminal_ (colors, tables, spinners — `crates/cli/src/output.rs`'s comfy-table helpers, `indicatif` progress bars). A _serialization format_ — even a human-readable, LLM-optimized one like TOON — is a consumer-facing data contract, judged by "does another program or prompt consume this," not "is it pretty-printed." TOON is core-side because it's plumbed through `PipelineOptions`/pipeline output the same way canonical JSON is (`caliper_docgen_core::toon::render_output_toon(&output)` at `extract.rs:57`), and because a NAPI/plu

56 `PropType::is_literal_union()` (`crates/core/src/types/output.rs:365`):

77 RDT natively supports a `composes: string[]` field on each component — "these props come from this named type, listed by reference, not flattened into `props`." This tool's resolver reuses that exact mechanism for a second, distinct purpose: recording every type it gave up trying to resolve. `ResolvedChain::give_up` (`crates/core/src/resolver/mod.rs:380-386`) is "the sanctioned 'give up' entry point for every 'this type couldn't be followed further, stop here' path" — it pushes an optional `Diagnostic` and then calls `empty_with_compose(type_name)`, which sets `composes: vec![type_name]`. Every unresolvable type (a conditional type, a generic pattern the resolver doesn't understand, a cycle)

113 `truncate_with_indicator(parts: &[String], limit: usize, sep: &str) -> String` (`toon.rs:97-104`) is the single shared helper for "cut a member list down to `limit` items, and if anything was cut, say so":

136 Every `PropType` variant has an explicit match arm in `format_type_compact` (`toon.rs:107-150`) — there is no wildcard `_ => ...` catch-all. `PropType::Object(_)` and `PropType::Tuple(_)` delegate to `raw_string()` rather than a bespoke compact form (both can be arbitrarily nested/structured, so a hand-written compact form isn't obviously better than the existing raw renderer). `PropType::Opaque(detail)` renders as `opaque(<raw of the opaque detail>)`.

148 `schema_covers_every_field_name_the_real_output_serializes` (`schema.rs:117-211`) is the only guard against `schema_value()` silently falling out of sync with the real structs. Read honestly, its actual coverage boundary is narrower than "the schema matches the real output":

59 `PropType` and `CollectedType` do **not** derive `Serialize`/`Deserialize`. Each hand-writes the round-trip through a private `to_json_value`/`from_json_value` pair that builds/reads a `serde_json::Value` directly (`output.rs:436-715`, `collected.rs:209-461`), then wires that into the `serde::Serialize`/`serde::Deserialize` traits by hand.

65 **Correction to the ADR itself, verified against current code (2026-08):** ADR-0002 states "`PropType`, `CollectedType`, and `OpaqueReason` don't derive Serialize/Deserialize." This is stale for `OpaqueReason`. The current source (`output.rs:743-745`) shows:

81 `OpaqueReason` derives normally. It isn't recursive — every variant's payload is a `String` or a unit — so it never hit the recursion-limit problem the ADR is about. The _serialization of an `OpaqueReason` value_ is still hand-assembled inside `PropType::to_tagged_value`'s `Opaque` arm (`output.rs:538-567`, matching each reason to its own `serde_json::json!{...}` shape) and hand-parsed in `from_tagged_value` (`output.rs:687-711`) — but that's because it's embedded inside `PropType`'s own manual impl, not because `OpaqueReason` itself needs one. This is a small, real documentation bug in ADR-0002 worth a one-line fix, independent of anything else in this file.

89 **Why it's load-bearing:** a derived serde impl gives you a compiler error the moment you add a new enum variant and forget to handle it in serialization. A hand-written match loses that safety net _unless every match stays exhaustive_ — a wildcard arm would silently absorb a new variant into whatever the wildcard does (often `Opaque` or a panic), and nothing would tell you serialization is now lossy for that variant. `to_tagged_value` (output.rs:451-568) and `from_tagged_value` (output.rs:576-712), and `to_json_value`/`from_json_value` in `collected.rs`, are all written this way. If you add a `PropType` variant, the compiler _will_ fail the exhaustiveness check in `to_tagged_value` and force you to handle it — but only because nobody put a wildcard there. Adding one defeats the entire safety mechanism this ADR relies on.

99 **Source:** `crates/core/src/types/output.rs:316-357`, cross-referenced against call sites in `crates/core/src/known.rs` and `crates/core/src/resolver/*.rs`

124 - `known.rs` — every call is `OpaqueDetail::new`, for the documented exception: `known.rs` has no `ResolveState` of its own to push a diagnostic onto (it's a lookup table, not a resolution pass), so it pushes its diagnostic separately through `push_known_opaque_diagnostic` (`known.rs:31`) at the call site that invokes the lookup, rather than inline in the constructor.

131 **Source:** `crates/core/src/types/output.rs:118-210`

154 **Invariant 4:** a `ParsedProp` can never exist with `required: true` and `default_value: Some(_)` simultaneously. `ParsedProp::new` (output.rs:159-171) enforces this by construction:

196 **`DiagnosticCode::Unknown` is intentional dead code, not a gap.** Its doc comment (diagnostic.rs:65-70) states it: reserved headroom for external consumers constructing their own `Diagnostic` outside the extraction pipeline (e.g. a wrapping tool). Nothing in `crates/core` or `crates/cli` is expected to construct it, and it shows up in this crate's own tests only as a placeholder value (`output.rs` tests build `Diagnostic { code: DiagnosticCode::Unknown, .. }` when the specific code doesn't matter to the assertion). Do not "clean this up" by removing it as unused — that's the entire point of it existing.

200 **Invariant 5:** `DiagnosticSeverity` has no derived `Ord` — `max_severity()` on `ExtractionOutput` (output.rs:33-35) ranks severities explicitly via a private `severity_rank` function (`Error` = 2, `Warning` = 1, `Info` = 0) rather than relying on enum declaration order. The doc comment is explicit about why: declaration order isn't a promise about severity ranking, and a future contributor reordering the enum's variants (e.g. alphabetizing) would silently invert exit-code behavior if ranking were derived from `Ord`. `exit_code(strict: bool)` (output.rs:42-55) is the single shared mapping reused as-is by `extract`, `watch`, `check --strict`, and `inspect` in the CLI — changing this mapping changes exit-code behavior for every subcommand at once, not just one.

204 **Source:** `crates/core/src/types/output.rs:11-232`

244 **Invariant 8:** `composes: Vec<String>` holds type names that could not be resolved, explicitly for react-docgen compatibility (doc comment, output.rs:102). This is the "stop-gap" mechanism referenced in recent commit history (`df769ee feat(resolver): surface unresolvable props via react-docgen's own composes field`) — when the resolver can't expand an inherited type into concrete props, rather than silently dropping that inheritance layer's props from the output, it names the type in `composes` so a consumer already handling RDT's `composes` field (a well-known RDT quirk) gets equivalent information instead of silent data loss.

246 `ComponentEntry::html_element()` (output.rs:113-115) derives the rendered HTML element from `inheritance`, taking the _first_ layer with `html_element: Some(_)` via `find_map`. This means inheritance order matters for this lookup even though it isn't independently validated anywhere in this file — if a component's inheritance chain somehow had two HTML-attribute layers, the outermost one wins by construction, not by any explicit precedence rule.

250 **Source:** `crates/core/src/types/output.rs:785-797`

258 `GlobalSourceData` is the merged, cross-file view built once during pipeline orchestration and then read (never mutated) by all parallel resolver workers — `crates/core/AGENTS.md`'s "Resolver" section states it's used via `Arc` in the pipeline specifically so `.clone()` stays cheap. All its maps key by `"${absolute_file_path}:${name}"` (scoped, never bare) — `interfaces`, `type_aliases`, `type_alias_params`, `interface_type_params`, `enums`, `const_arrays` all share this convention, which is what makes `remove_file()` (global.rs:100-111) correct: it can drop every entry belonging to one file with a single `prefix = "{file_path}:"` + `retain(|k, _| !k.starts_with(&prefix))` per map, without needing a reverse index.

260 **Invariant 9:** `GlobalSourceData::merge()` (global.rs:75-97) performs TypeScript declaration merging for interfaces specifically — if a key already exists (an interface with the same scoped key was already merged, e.g. from a second file augmenting the same module), it _extends_ `props` and `extends` on the existing entry rather than overwriting it (global.rs:78-83). Every other field (`type_aliases`, `enums`, `const_arrays`, ...) uses plain `HashMap::extend`, which _does_ overwrite on key collision. This asymmetry is deliberate — TypeScript interfaces support declaration merging as a language feature; type aliases, enums, and const arrays don't, so a colliding key for those really is either a bug (duplicate scoped key) or an intentional last-write-wins re-parse (e.g. cache invalidation re-merging an updated file after `remove_file()`).

262 `ResolveState` (global.rs:19-30) is `pub(crate)`, not `pub` — it never crosses into `ExtractionOutput` or any consumer-facing type. It bundles `visited` (cycle detection, `"${file}:${type_name}"` keys), `diagnostics` (accumulated during one `resolve_component()` call), and `in_scope_type_params` (generic placeholder tracking). AGENTS.md's "Resolver" section states explicitly: "`ResolveState` accumulates diagnostics and visited-type tracking for a single resolution call; it is not shared" — each parallel rayon worker gets its own, freshly created per component, never reused or merged across components.

286 This is also _why_ `CollectedObjectField` (collected.rs:469-475) still plainly derives `Serialize`/`Deserialize` rather than getting folded into `CollectedType`'s manual impl, and why its own test (`collected_object_field_round_trips_through_rmp_serde_positional_encoding`, collected.rs:765-780) exists specifically to exercise `visit_seq` (positional) deserialization rather than `visit_map` — it's the one path that would actually break if someone "simplified" it into a map-based encoding, since `CollectedType`'s own hand-rolled (de)serialization never calls into `CollectedObjectField`'s derive at all (it builds fields manually inside `to_json_value`/`from_json_value`); the derive only matters for whatever _does_ serialize a bare `CollectedObjectField`, which today is exactly this rmp_serde cache path.
